evidence.notes: Steady-state prod-only loadout. Baseline for all co-residency comparisons.

Drill runtime bound alongside the resident prod LLM: the previously paper-only co-residency question, now measured. Both sides served correctly; the 128K runtime completed a 72025-token prompt; VRAM headroom ~0.5%.
Measured co-residency attempt: 35B interactive + 5.75 GiB prod model.

outcomes.declared_file_size_gap: model is 16.2 GB on disk but 22.09 GiB resident

loadouts.description: Smallest loadout that keeps the production LLM path healthy.

Production LLM plus the 35B interactive resident. Measured infeasible on x1-370: the runtime cannot allocate the 35B while the prod model is resident, so the device is a choice, not a sum. Use studio_only when the operator wants the big model.
Drill runtime without speculation, alone: the production LLM yields the card.
Speculative drill runtime plus its draft model. The draft is a real resident: with the 3B production model loaded, binding this drill fails to allocate the draft and the runtime never starts.
Non-speculative drill runtime beside the production model. Measured: both served, including a 72025-token prompt on the 128K runtime.
Interactive lane only; production LLM path is degraded.
Nothing resident: maximum headroom, every LLM-need unmet.

models.load_note: Loaded in 9.72s; 5.75 GiB resident; completion median 0.478s over 5 samples.
models.vram_note: 5.75 GiB resident as measured by lms after load.

models.load_note: Bound repeatedly by bind-soak-runtime.sh and measured across 32 cases at 32K and 128K context, including a 72025-token prompt, with and without the production model resident. LM Studio loadability of this file has not been tested and is not implied.
`lms load k2-horizon-7b` (BF16 18.0 GB, arch k2-horizon) hung >600s and never appeared in `lms ps`; VRAM unchanged. Do not retry blindly on this runtime.

Loads alone in ~15s (22.09 GiB resident -- far above the 16.2 GB file size, which is what a size-based estimate would assume). Loading it alongside the 5.75 GiB prod model FAILS on this card: 'unable to allocate ROCm0 buffer'. It therefore requires the device to itself (exclusive_gpu).

Loads in seconds and serves completions, but passed only 1 of 8 representative task-quality cases (2026-09-30), so it is NOT a viable policy for the suite: the gate requires every case to pass. Recorded because it is the obvious cost lever for the 25k-state ladder and it fails on quality, not on throughput.

Speculative draft for the dflash runtime. With the 3B production model resident, binding r9700 dflash fails to load this draft ('unable to allocate') and the bind hangs until timeout, which is why the run looked like a policy failure and was in fact a capacity one. Its resident cost is estimated from file size and should be measured.
models.verified_in: soak-binder (fails to load alongside a resident prod model)

needs.description: Production AssistX LLM traffic needs the configured production model served on :1234 (role prod-llm). Any other large model is not a substitute: the app expects its configured LLM_MODEL.
Embeddings for AssistX request paths need a resident embedder.
Task-quality/soak drills bind an exclusive llama-server runtime.
Benchmark/eval replays need the same exclusive runtime as a drill.
An operator-facing interactive studio lane wants a capable resident model serving the interactive role (not the small production model).

note: Devices and model VRAM figures are measured facts. Loadout preferences are declared by an operator until measured outcomes for (circumstance, loadout) pairs exist.
notes: Device capacity is a choice, not arithmetic: on x1-370 (31.9 GiB) the 35B interactive model (22.09 GiB resident) and the 5.75 GiB production model cannot both be resident -- the runtime refuses the allocation even though the totals fit on paper. Models that need the device alone carry exclusive_gpu.

Ladder cost probe: the cheap runtime is not a shortcut. A 0.8B model serves the suite at a fraction of the cost and still fails the quality gate (1/8 representative cases), so scaling states means more cases or fewer options per state -- not a smaller model.
